chapter: Learning piano, dancing and Alphonso Trent
title: Charleston dancing builds stage confidence; studying with Mrs. Pittman
summary: Dancing the Charleston gives him confidence before an audience while he studies with Mrs. Pittman, who praises his feeling for the piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You were saying that dancing in front of people gave you confidence.

Yeah. Yeah, that's...we call it...I hear people call it stage fright, stage presence, you know, being before an audience, being afraid, being nervous, forgetting...if you sing, forget the words or if you're a dancer forgetting part of the routine, or a musician...well, that dancing did quite a bit for me. And it furthered my musical career. Because (our tendency with that?) I was studying with Mrs. Pittman by then.

She was a music teacher, yes. She was a school teacher and music, she taught music. So what I did was to study with her, you know, and then I would dance, you know, and the opportunity came to join Alphonso. Mrs. Pittman said to me when she first heard me touch the piano, you know, she wanted to see how I knew and how I could play little things. She said, "Sammy, you have an exceptional knowledge of the instrument. You know, and a good feeling. I don't know if you'll ever become a great reading musician, but you can share your
feeling with other musicians who are trained." That was exactly what she said to me, and I thought that was a pretty good compliment.
Yeah, but that's kind of unusual, because at that time music teachers were, you know...
